    StartersStab premiere caramel cornOven-baked caramel popcorn with salted peanuts, crisp and glassyHow to make it2 tbsp vegetable oil100g popcorn kernels100g salted peanuts100g butter150g brown sugar60ml golden syrup1/2 tsp salt1/2 tsp bicarb sodaHeat the oil in a big covered pot, add the kernels and shake constantly until the popping slows. Tip into a large roasting tin with the peanuts.Heat the oven to 120°C. Melt the butter with the brown sugar, golden syrup and salt, then boil without stirring.Take off the heat, stir in the bicarb soda, pour over the popcorn and toss well.Bake, stirring every 15 minutes.Spread on baking paper to cool, then break into clusters.Cici's sorority house dipHot spinach and artichoke dip with parmesan and mozzarella, baked bubbling, with pita chipsHow to make it4 pita breads2 tbsp olive oilsalt, a pinch250g frozen spinach, thawed280g jar marinated artichoke hearts, drained250g cream cheese, soft125g sour cream2 garlic cloves, crushed50g parmesan, grated100g mozzarella, gratedblack pepper, to tasteHeat the oven to 200°C. Cut the pita breads into wedges, toss with the olive oil and salt, and spread on a tray.Bake the pita wedges until crisp.Squeeze the spinach dry and chop the artichoke hearts.Mix the cream cheese, sour cream, garlic, parmesan and half the mozzarella, then stir in the spinach, artichokes and black pepper.Spread in a small baking dish, top with the rest of the mozzarella and bake until bubbling and golden.Rest, then serve with the pita chips.Loaded nachos with jalapeñosEaten through Derek's I Think I Love You.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsWindsor College Cincinnati chilliOhio-style spiced beef chilli over spaghetti, with kidney beans, onion and a mound of cheddarHow to make it750g beef mince1 L cold water3 onions, diced, one kept raw for the top3 garlic cloves, crushed140g tomato paste2 tbsp chilli powder2 tsp ground cinnamon2 tsp ground cumin1 tsp ground allspice1/4 tsp ground cloves1 tbsp cocoa powder2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce1 tbsp cider vinegar2 bay leaves1 1/2 tsp salt400g spaghetti400g tin kidney beans, drained200g cheddar, very finely grated100g small salted crackersPut the mince in a large pot with the cold water and break it up with a whisk until fine.Add two of the onions, the garlic, tomato paste, chilli powder, cinnamon, cumin, allspice, cloves, cocoa, Worcestershire, vinegar, bay leaves and salt, and bring to the boil.Simmer uncovered, stirring now and then, until thick but still saucy.Skim off the fat and take out the bay leaves.Meanwhile cook the spaghetti, warm the kidney beans and finely dice the last onion.Divide the spaghetti between four plates, ladle over the chilli and top with the beans, raw onion and a mound of cheddar. Serve with the crackers.Opening night chicken souvlakiSidney as Cassandra in the college's Greek tragedy, with a chorus in masksHow to make it800g chicken thigh fillets2 lemons2 tsp dried oregano3 garlic cloves60ml olive oil250g Greek yoghurt1 Lebanese cucumber3 tomatoes1 red onion150g feta4 pita breadsCut the chicken into chunks and toss with the juice of 1 lemon, the oregano, 2 crushed garlic cloves, half the oil and salt. Thread onto skewers.Grate half the cucumber, squeeze it out and mix with the yoghurt, the last garlic clove and salt.Chop the tomatoes, the rest of the cucumber and the onion, top with feta and dress with the rest of the oil and lemon.Grill the skewers on a hot grill for 10 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.Warm the pita and serve with the skewers, tzatziki and salad.SweetsWindsor College buckeyesPeanut butter balls half dipped in dark chocolate, kept coldHow to make it250g smooth peanut butter60g butter, soft1 tsp vanilla extractsalt, a pinch250g icing sugar250g dark chocolate, chopped1 tsp coconut oilBeat the peanut butter, butter, vanilla and salt, then work in the icing sugar.Roll into 2.5cm balls on a lined tray.Freeze until firm.Melt the dark chocolate with the coconut oil over simmering water.Spear each ball with a toothpick and dip in the chocolate, leaving a circle of peanut butter showing on top. Smooth over the hole with a finger.Chill until set.DrinksFrat party cherry bourbon smashBourbon shaken with muddled cherries, mint and lemon over crushed iceHow to make it60g caster sugar60ml hot water200g pitted cherries, fresh or frozen1 bunch mint240ml bourbon80ml lemon juice, from 2 lemons4 cups crushed iceStir the sugar into the hot water until dissolved, then cool.Muddle the cherries with a handful of mint leaves and the syrup in a shaker.Add the bourbon, lemon juice and a scoop of ice and shake hard, in two batches.Strain over crushed ice in four tumblers and top each with a cherry and a mint sprig.Zima with a Jolly RancherFrat house pour, before the party gets loud.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
